replaced_paragraphs.before: Leakage Aware State of Health Estimation for Lithium Ion Batteries with Cross Battery and Cross Dataset Validation
replaced_paragraphs.after: State of Health Estimation and Target Leakage Auditing for Lithium Ion Batteries

replaced_paragraphs.before: Abstract—Accurate state-of-health (SOH) estimation requires inputs available when an estimate is made and testing on batteries excluded from fitting. We compare 20 regressors using 18 scalar features or 64 × 5 sequences from the observable 4.0–3.6 V discharge segment. NASA uses disjoint training, validation, and test batteries over five folds and three seeds; CALCE and Oxford provide separate grouped evaluations and untouched zero-shot targets for NASA-trained models. A factorial audit shows that current-cycle target proxies reduce grouped ExtraTrees MAE from 4.145 to 0.436 SOH percentage points (pp). Under the corrected protocol, the Weighted Average Ensemble has the lowest NASA battery-macro MAE (3.536 pp); its averaged held-out predictions yield sample MAE 3.682 pp, RMSE 6.011 pp, MAPE 4.37%, R² 0.610, adjusted R² 0.607, and 79.2% within ±5 absolute SOH pp. The best frozen NASA models obtain MAE 6.955 pp on CALCE and 4.615 pp on Oxford, much worse than the respective within-dataset fits. Secondary NASA health-band diagnostics use validation-residual scores; capacity/RUL trajectories are retrospective descriptions with censoring. These laboratory results support leakage-aware benchmarking, not a validated charging policy or field deployment.

These laboratory results support leakage-aware benchmarking, not a validated charging policy or field deployment.

replaced_paragraphs.before: This study makes five contributions. It defines a leakage-safe current-cycle SOH task using only a fixed partial-discharge window; evaluates eight classical, ten sequence, and two ensemble models using disjoint train, validation, and test batteries; quantifies split and target-proxy effects in a V1/V2/V3 factorial audit; and tests both grouped within-dataset performance and zero-shot NASA-to-CALCE/Oxford transfer. A secondary NASA analysis evaluates SOH-derived health bands and reports censoring-aware descriptive capacity/RUL trajectories. The software is supplied as a reproducible research prototype. Charging recommendations are outside the validated endpoint and are not claimed as an operational control policy.
replaced_paragraphs.after: This study makes five contributions. It defines a leakage-safe current-cycle SOH task using only a fixed partial-discharge window; evaluates eight classical, ten sequence, and two ensemble models using disjoint train, validation, and test batteries; audits split sensitivity and target-proxy leakage using V1/V2/V3 comparisons plus paired sample-count, predictor-count and temperature-quota controls; and tests both grouped within-dataset performance and zero-shot NASA-to-CALCE/Oxford transfer. A secondary NASA analysis evaluates SOH-derived health bands and reports censoring-aware descriptive capacity/RUL trajectories. The software is supplied as a reproducible research prototype. Charging recommendations are outside the validated endpoint and are not claimed as an operational control policy.
replaced_paragraphs.reason: Narrow contribution to supported audit findings

replaced_paragraphs.before: We reconstruct three split designs and cross each with either the safe 18-feature contract or four legacy target proxies: current capacity retention, current cumulative capacity, current capacity difference, and a rolling mean containing current SOH. V1 randomly holds out cycles, V2 holds out the final 20% of each battery chronologically, and V3 holds out complete batteries. The comparison uses the same Extra Trees estimator, eliminating architecture as an explanation for metric differences.
replaced_paragraphs.after: We reconstruct three split designs using the same ExtraTrees hyperparameters. Each compares the 18 observable features with those same 18 plus four deliberately invalid current-target proxies. V1 randomly holds out cycles; V2 holds out the final 20% of retained rows within each battery; V3 holds out whole batteries. This is a split-by-input diagnostic, not a causal decomposition: training counts, exposure composition, and test populations differ between protocols. Table 2 and Fig. 8 retain the original audit; the added controls in Section VII-C address sample and predictor count and training-temperature composition. They do not make the cross-protocol test populations exchangeable.

replaced_paragraphs.before: Tree ensembles use 250–400 estimators with fixed seed, and scaled SVR, ridge, and seven-neighbour distance-weighted KNN serve as non-tree baselines. Recurrent models use two 64-unit layers. PyTorch transformer models use dimension 64, four heads, and two blocks; TensorFlow iTransformer variants use dimension 32, four heads, and two blocks. VAE-LSTM uses a 16-dimensional latent state with up to 30 warm-up epochs. Neural optimization uses Adam at 10^-3 with MAE-based validation; the physics-informed auxiliary head has loss weight 0.3. Batch size is 64. These fixed settings are shared across datasets rather than retuned on external labels.
replaced_paragraphs.after: Tree ensembles use 250–400 estimators with fixed seed, and scaled SVR, ridge, and seven-neighbour distance-weighted KNN serve as non-tree baselines. Recurrent models use two 64-unit layers. PyTorch transformer models use dimension 64, four heads, and two blocks; TensorFlow iTransformer variants use dimension 32, four heads, and two blocks. VAE-LSTM uses a 16-dimensional latent state with up to 30 warm-up epochs. Neural optimization uses Adam at 10^-3. Ordinary PyTorch models stop on mean validation-batch MAE after training-target normalization. VAE-LSTM stops on reconstruction plus annealed KL and health-prediction loss; the physics-informed TensorFlow model stops on the weighted validation loss of both heads (auxiliary weight 0.3). These monitored objectives are not identical to the raw SOH MAE reported for evaluation. Batch size is 64. These fixed settings are shared across datasets rather than retuned on external labels.
replaced_paragraphs.reason: Report the actual model-specific stopping objectives

replaced_paragraphs.before: NASA and Oxford use five outer battery-grouped folds; CALCE uses four because it has only four cells. In each outer fold, a grouped 20% of the remaining cells forms validation data. Seeds 17, 42, and 2026 repeat partitioning and initialization. Model selection minimizes mean per-battery MAE. For headline sample metrics, repeated held-out predictions for each record are averaged first and metrics are recomputed on those records. We distinguish that estimand from the mean of separate fold metrics. MAE = mean(|y − ŷ|), RMSE = √mean((y − ŷ)²), R² = 1 − SSE/SST, and within-5-pp coverage = mean(1[|y − ŷ| ≤ 5]). Adjusted R² uses p = 18 and is descriptive rather than a valid neural-network complexity correction. We also report MAPE, median and 95th-percentile absolute error, signed bias, residuals, and fold-level training versus held-out-battery gaps. Training MAE is in-sample and is not an unbiased validation score. All absolute errors are SOH percentage points; within-5 coverage is not R².

replaced_paragraphs.before: Within-dataset results retrain every model using grouped folds on CALCE or Oxford. Zero-shot results train and select models only on NASA; the fitted preprocessing and model are then frozen and applied to all target records. CALCE and Oxford labels are accessed only for final scoring. No target-domain fine-tuning, calibration, threshold selection, or feature normalization is permitted.
replaced_paragraphs.after: Within-dataset results retrain every model using grouped folds on CALCE or Oxford. Zero-shot results train and select models only on NASA; the fitted preprocessing and model are then frozen and applied to all target records. CALCE and Oxford labels are accessed only for final scoring. No target-domain fine-tuning, calibration, threshold selection, or feature normalization is permitted. Freezing includes the source-fitted median imputer, any scalar/channel standardization, training-target normalization, ensemble weights and stacking coefficients. Interpolation inside an observed partial segment is a fixed per-record operation with no pooled target-domain fit. Ambient temperature is numeric in degrees Celsius and temperature_observed is binary; neither uses a target-fitted encoder. Section IV-G gives the complete preprocessing contract.

replaced_paragraphs.before: For the selected NASA model, 10,000 battery-cluster bootstrap resamples give sample MAE 3.682 pp with a 95% interval of 1.879–5.966 pp and within-5 coverage 79.2% with a 61.4–94.4% interval (Fig. 23). Paired battery-level Wilcoxon tests with Holm adjustment reject equal MAE in 13 of 19 comparisons at adjusted p < 0.05. The comparison with the released SVR model is not significant (adjusted p = 0.824). Across 15 folds, the Weighted Average Ensemble has mean in-sample training MAE 0.562 pp versus held-out-battery MAE 3.779 pp, a 3.217 pp generalization gap. This substantial gap cautions against interpreting a fitted training score as deployment performance. Fold-level gaps, residuals, and predictions are supplied with the reproducibility artifacts; no single R² score substitutes for these checks.

replaced_paragraphs.before: The principal result is methodological. Changing only the split moves safe-feature Extra Trees MAE from less than one point to more than four points, and adding current-label proxies almost eliminates error even with held-out cells. Thus an impressive tolerance coverage can coexist with an invalid information pathway. The corrected benchmark estimates the harder question: whether an observable partial discharge predicts current SOH on a physically unseen battery.
replaced_paragraphs.after: The principal result is methodological. The original diagnostic reports safe-feature ExtraTrees MAE below one point for random-cycle testing and above four points for held-out-battery testing, but these tests differ in populations, histories and exposure composition. The matched controls in Fig. 25 narrow the within-split conclusion: access to current-target proxies lowers error far more than adding equally many shuffled proxies on the same sampled training and test rows. This demonstrates an invalid information pathway; it does not assign a causal MAE penalty to grouping alone. The corrected benchmark estimates whether an observable partial discharge predicts retrospective current SOH on a physically unseen battery.
